title: Implement GL8-GL12 Authorization Pipeline for Human Gate Integrity
context: PHASE 5.0-C Runtime Enforcement Investigation identified 5 critical authorization enforcement gaps in GovernancePipeline.before_tool(). Decision Ledger integrity, scope binding, content integrity, tool registry, and encoding validation are currently missing, allowing unauthorized tool executions.

alternatives.rejected_reason: Architectural debt, poor maintainability, monolithic bloat
Partial selection only - incomplete without orchestration
Partial selection only - incomplete without modular engines
N/A - Selected as approved approach

decision: Implement GL8-GL12 Authorization Pipeline using Option 2+3 Hybrid approach: independent governance engines (GL8-GL12) orchestrated by dedicated AuthorizationPipeline, integrated as pre-check in GovernancePipeline.before_tool().
rationale: Hybrid approach combines modular architecture (each layer independent & testable) with clear orchestration (authorization as separate gate before GL1-GL7). Provides fast-fail authorization, extensibility for future GL13+, and clean separation of concerns. All 5 FAIL scenarios covered by GL8-GL12 verification contracts.
impact: New files: 6 modules (5 engines + 1 pipeline). Schema extensions: Decision Ledger (authorized_scope, decision_content_hash), Tool Metadata registry. Implementation timeline: 10-16 hours across 6 phases. Backward compatibility: graceful handling of existing authorization records.

title: PHASE 5.1-A Remediation Design Approval (HGD-C1/A1/B1)
context: PHASE 5.1-A Implementation Verification (commit 916bef7) identified three blocking gaps in the GL8-GL12 Authorization Pipeline: GAP-2 (Authorization Context Propagation - all write tools blocked at GL8_FAIL_1 because decision_id is not conveyed in args), GAP-5 (Tool Registry Coverage - 6 critical write tools missing from GL11 TOOL_REGISTRY), GAP-3 (Integration Test Execution - all 15+ integration tests are pass stubs). Three Human Gate Decision Packages (HGD-C1, HGD-A1, HGD-B1) were prepared and reviewed. Status: DESIGN REVIEW COMPLETE.

decision: APPROVED with conditions. Selected options: HGD-C1 X2 (FAIL_1 + Happy Path as minimum verification criterion), HGD-A1 Option B+A (READ_ONLY_TOOLS bypass + _authz envelope for write tools), HGD-B1 Option B (JSON schema file at data/governance/tool_registry.json). Implementation requires separate authorization. Runtime activation requires separate verification gate. No authority expansion.
rationale: Option B+A for HGD-A1: READ bypass reuses existing READ_ONLY_TOOLS set (zero regression for read operations); _authz envelope adds per-operation authorization traceability for write tools; both within approved DC_20261002_GL8_GL12_ARCHITECTURE scope. Option B for HGD-B1: JSON file is auditable in git, enables non-code governance maintenance, fail-closed on load failure. X2 for HGD-C1: FAIL_1 + Happy Path verifies both DENY and ALLOW paths without requiring GAP-2/5 resolution.
impact: Unblocks PHASE 5.1-A implementation execution when separately authorized. Execution order: Step 1 (C1 Stage 1 - independent), Step 2 (A1+B1+GAP-4 BOM fix - combined commit), Step 3 (C1 Stage 2+ - after Step 2), Step 4 (Production deployment - separate Human Gate required). Does not activate Runtime Enforcement until Step 4 gate.

title: HGD-A1 Implementation Scope Authorization: B+A Combined (READ bypass + _authz envelope)
context: PHASE 5.1-A GAP-2/GAP-4 remediation. GAP-2: GL8 reads args.get("decision_id") directly — no current MoCKA tool passes this field, blocking all write operations at GL8_FAIL_1. GAP-4: governance_pipeline.py in commit 916bef7 has UTF-8 BOM contamination. C1 Stage 1 verified both blocking and happy-path behavior of the GL8-GL12 pipeline (PHASE5_1_A_C1_STAGE1_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md). Design decision: B+A combined approach selected per HGDR_HGD_A1_20261002 Rev.2. References: DC_20261002_PHASE5_1_A_REMEDIATION, HGDR_HGD_A1_20261002.

alternatives.rejected_reason: Architectural expansion beyond approved scope; session lifecycle management requires new module; compromised session could execute all authorized writes
Requires GAP-5 registry completion as prerequisite; higher dependency chain risk; changes security model

alternatives.option: Option A alone (_authz envelope only, no READ bypass)
alternatives.rejected_reason: Read tools still blocked at GL8_FAIL_1 without decision_id — operational regression for all read operations

decision: Authorize implementation of HGD-A1 B+A combined approach within the scope defined in HGDR_HGD_A1_20261002 Rev.2: (1) authorization_pipeline.py: add READ_ONLY_TOOLS bypass at entry of execute() (~+15 lines); (2) human_gate_authorization_integrity.py: read from args["_authz"]["decision_id"] instead of args["decision_id"] (~+5 lines); (3) authorization_scope_binding.py: read from args["_authz"]["scope"] instead of args["scope"] (~+3 lines); (4) governance_pipeline.py: strip UTF-8 BOM (GAP-4, 0 logic changes). Class-based Authorization Context Separation enforced: READ_ONLY_TOOLS (Class A) bypass pipeline; WRITE_TOOLS (Class B) require _authz envelope. Human Gate authority chain preserved: Human Gate Decision -> Decision Ledger -> _authz reference. AI self-generation of _authz authority prohibited.
rationale: C1 Stage 1 PASS confirms GL8-GL12 pipeline correctness (both FAIL_1 fast-fail and AUTHZ_OK happy-path verified). B+A resolves GAP-2 (write tools unblocked via _authz envelope) and GAP-4 (BOM contamination) without breaking read operations or changing GL8-GL12 verification algorithms. READ_ONLY_TOOLS reuses existing governance_pipeline.py set — no new module required. Per-operation authorization traceability preserved via explicit _authz envelope on each write call.
impact: Scope limited to 4 files: authorization_pipeline.py, human_gate_authorization_integrity.py, authorization_scope_binding.py, governance_pipeline.py (BOM strip only). GL8-GL12 verification algorithms unchanged. No new modules. No runtime activation. Read operations: zero regression (AUTHZ_BYPASS_READ_ONLY). Write operations: unblocked when valid _authz provided. Without _authz: still blocked at GL8_FAIL_1 (security contract preserved).

decision: Authorize implementation of HGD-B1 JSON Schema Registry within the scope defined in HGDR_HGD_B1_20261002: (1) structural/tool_registry_enforcement.py: replace hardcoded TOOL_REGISTRY dict with _load_registry() JSON file loader (~+25 lines, -11 hardcoded entries); (2) data/governance/tool_registry.json: new file with tool entries (17 estimated; final count after KUROKO PC 照合). context: HGD-A1 (DC_20261002_HGD_A1_IMPLEMENTATION_SCOPE, Active) and HGD-B1 (DC_20261002_HGD_B1_IMPLEMENTATION_SCOPE, Active) defined the design and scope of GL8-GL12 Authorization Pipeline remediation for GAP-2/4/5. decision: Authorize KUROKO to implement A1+B1 combined code changes on the KUROKO PC following the 10-step execution order defined in HGDR_HGD_D1_20261002: (1) Registry completeness 照合, (2) .gitignore audit, (3) CHANGE_START, (4) A1 implementation (4 files), (5) B1 implementation (2 files), (6) UTF-8/BOM verification, (7) CHANGE_DONE, (8) KUROKO PC Read-Back, (9) Human Gate report, (10) commit/push after acknowledgement. commit/push is NOT an implementation completion condition — it follows Human Gate report.
